campbell.title: Campbell City Council — August 18, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered routine business including approval of past meeting minutes, payment of city bills, and acceptance of a donation from the Campbell Police Foundation for K9 support. The Council also reviewed new labor agreements with two employee groups, a bond oversight committee report, and administrative items like conference delegate designation and a city clerk contract amendment.
keyTopics: Acceptance of $41,911.62 in Campbell Police Foundation donations for K9 veterinarian services and equipment
New two-year labor agreements (2026-2028) with the Campbell Peace Officers Association and the North Coast States Carpenters Union
FY 2025 Annual Report from the Citizen's Bond Oversight Committee for Measure O
Designation of voting delegates for the League of California Cities Annual Conference
Resolution amending the City Clerk services agreement to provide a merit increase

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — August 19, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered a routine mix of contracts and administrative items, including janitorial services, irrigation maintenance, a GIS consultant amendment, and playground replacement at Bellgrove Park. The Council also took up a contested appeal involving a proposed 25-lot residential subdivision on Pierce Road, a new five-year law enforcement contract with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office, and several final map approvals for lot splits around the city.
keyTopics: Appeal of the Planning Commission's decision not to certify an Environmental Impact Report and denial of Design Review and a Tentative Map for a 25-lot subdivision on Pierce Road
Five-year law enforcement services agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office
Contracts for Bellgrove Park playground replacement with SpecPlay and Playgrounds Unlimited
No Parking Anytime zone on Chester Avenue and Arcadia Palms Drive
Purchase of electrical equipment to replace gas systems at Warner Hutton House, Civic Center Theater, and Joan Pisani Community Center

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — August 25, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered routine business including the History Museum roof replacement contract, EV chargers for the maintenance yard, and completion of the Woodland Library patio project. The Council also held a public hearing on a resident petition to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street and considered vesting tentative maps for new condominium developments at 349 First Street and at Sherwood/Acacia Avenues.
keyTopics: Public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, with options to act directly or refer to the Historical Commission for further study
Vesting tentative map for 19 condominium units at 349 First Street
Vesting tentative map for 33 condominium units at Sherwood and Acacia Avenues
Contract award for History Museum roof replacement with Diablo Roofing, not to exceed $147,500 plus contingency
Construction contract for the Maintenance Yard EV Chargers Project with Bockmon & Woody Electric Co., not to exceed $363,220

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council took up routine administrative business, including approving prior meeting minutes, financial reports, and payroll records, along with a professional services agreement and an amendment to an existing contract. The Council also considered an omnibus ordinance updating minor sections of the Town Code, appointed a voting delegate for the League of California Cities Annual conference, and addressed a request related to continuing or hearing a public hearing appeal.
keyTopics: Monthly financial and investment report for June 2026
Professional services agreement authorization for the Town Manager
Second amendment to an existing agreement
Omnibus ordinance making minor updates to the Town Code
Voting delegate and alternate appointment for the League of California Cities Annual conference

san-jose.title: San José City Council — August 26, 2026
san-jose.summary: This was primarily an administrative Rules and Open Government Committee meeting, focused on setting the agenda for the City Council's September 1, 2026 meeting and canceling the September 8, 2026 meeting. The committee also considered an appointment to the VEBA Advisory Committee and a joint special meeting with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee.
keyTopics: Setting the final agenda for the September 1, 2026 City Council meeting
Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 draft agenda
Review of the public record for August 13-20, 2026
VEBA Advisory Committee appointment
Joint special meeting with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — August 25, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council took public comment on topics not otherwise on the agenda, then met in closed session to discuss performance evaluations for its two Council-appointed positions, the City Clerk and City Manager. The Council also discussed labor negotiations involving these unrepresented employees, with the Vice Mayor designated as the negotiator.
keyTopics: Public comment on non-agenda items
Performance evaluations of the City Clerk and City Manager
Labor negotiations regarding unrepresented employees (City Clerk and City Manager)

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting that began with a closed session followed by a public presentation. The presentation portion covered an update on the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session (special meeting)
CleanWater Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss plans for a Bike Fest event, a program addressing juvenile traffic diversion, and a presentation from a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI. The Commission also reviewed minutes from its June 10, 2026 meeting.
keyTopics: Bike Fest planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program
Presentation from youth-led organization Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, allowing both in-person and remote participation, with one Councilmember joining remotely from India. The agenda excerpt provided does not detail specific policy items or votes considered by the Council.
keyTopics: Hybrid meeting format with remote participation options via Zoom and phone
Councilmember Chahal participating remotely from Panchkula, India

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 11, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered introducing an ordinance amending a section of the municipal code, and received an educational presentation on the basics of municipal bonds. The meeting also included routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and reviewing the council's upcoming meeting calendar and agenda items.
keyTopics: Proposed ordinance to amend Municipal Code Title XIII, Chapters B.6
Educational presentation on municipal bonds basics
Review of upcoming City Council meeting calendar
Approval of prior City Council meeting minutes
Preview of anticipated items for the next regular Council meeting

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Public Art Commission — August 20, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Public Art Commission reviewed a plan for public art at a private development at 3150 El Camino Real, with a presentation from the project's art consultant, artist, and developer. The Commission also considered funding for temporary interactive media art installations and the acceptance of donated artworks for the city's public art collection.
keyTopics: Approval of June 18, 2026 meeting minutes
Public art plan and artist presentation for 3150 El Camino Real development
Proposed allocation of up to $70,000 for Code:ART 2027 interactive media installations
Acceptance of donated artworks by CASP artists Adrienne Defendi and Eric Fei
